41942.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I : If a capillary tube is immersed first in cold water and then in hot water, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in hot water. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate from the options given b
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
41942.sol: For water, the surface tension decreases as the temperature increases. At higher temperatures, the water molecules have more kinetic energy and are better able to overcome the cohesive forces at the surface, resulting in a decrease in surface tension. So, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in hot water and larger in cold water. Hence, statement I is true, but statement II is false.

70887.subject: Biology
70887.text: Which one of the following is INCORRECT about root hairs?
options: They are cytoplasmic extensions of epiblema cells.
70887.sol: Root hairs are unicellular, unbranched, and delicate tubular extensions of the epiblema (epidermal) cells of the root. They are found in the zone of maturation and are short-lived (ephemeral) structures. As the root grows, older root hairs die and new ones are continuously formed. Therefore, the statement that root hairs are permanent is incorrect. Answer: They are permanent.

71135.subject: Biology
71135.text: Which of the following is NOT a vector borne disease?
71135.sol: Malaria is a vector-borne disease transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito. Dengue is a vector-borne disease transmitted by the female Aedes mosquito. Filariasis is a vector-borne disease transmitted by the female Culex mosquito. Ascariasis is an intestinal infection caused by the parasitic roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides. It is transmitted through the ingestion of infective eggs from contaminated soil, water, or food, and does not involve any vector. Answer: Ascariasis

71739.text: Which atoms from EDTA are used to bind to metal ions during formation of complex?

Three nitrogen and three oxygen atoms
Four oxygen and two nitrogen atoms
Three oxygen, two nitrogen and one magnesium atoms
71739.sol: EDTA (Ethylenediaminetetraacetate) is a hexadentate ligand. Its chemical structure contains two nitrogen atoms and four carboxylate groups. After the ovulation, the granulosa cell as well as the stroma cells form theca interna rapidly multiply to fill the cavity of graafian follicle which becomes corpus luteum. If fertilization occurs, corpus luteum grows further and secrete hormone progesterone. If fertilization does not take place, corpus luteum regresses and forms a white body called corpus albicans.

84860.subject: Zoology
84860.text: DNA Polymorphism forms the basis of:
options: Both genetic mapping and DNA finger printing
84860.sol: As polymorphism in DNA sequence is the basis of genetic mapping of human genome as well as of DNA fingerprinting. Polymorphism (variation at genetic level) arises due to mutations. New mutations may arise in an individual either in somatic cells or in the germ cells. If a germ cell mutation does not seriously impair individual’s ability to have offspring who can transmit the mutation, it can spread to the other members of population (through sexual reproduction).

85467.subject: Zoology

85467.text: Which endangered animal is the source of the world's finest, lightest, warmest and most expensive wool-the shahtoosh?
85467.sol: Shahtoosh comes from the short, warm fleece of the rare Tibetan antelope (Pantholops hodgsonii - Chiru), a species found almost exclusively in the Changtang area of Tibet, on the Tibetan Plateau. It takes four animals to provide enough wool for just one shahtoosh shawl or scarf. Related Theory Despite legal protection of the highest order, the population of chiru is constantly on the decline and today the species is extremely endangered.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
85479.sol: Option (2) is the answer as both Statement I and Statement II are false because in cockroach the first pair of wings arises from mesothorax and not from prothorax. Moreover they are opaque, dark and leathery and not transparent as mentioned in Statement I Statement II is incorrect as the hind wings in cockroach are transparent, membranous and are metathoracic in origin.

85565.subject: Zoology

Calcitonin is secreted by thyroid gland. Melanin is secreted by dermal cells. Related Theory Mast cells contribute to homeostasis in the immune system. They serve as a first line of defense against antigens entering the body due to their location in the skin and mucosa.

Option (c) is the correct option as in ( i ) , ( ii ) and ( iv ) the state changes towards more random state, thus entropy increases.

123721.subject: Botany

These arms are held together at a point called the centromere (or primary constriction). Centromere occurs any where along the length of chromosome. During cell division spindle fibres are attached to centromere and help in the movement of chromosomes towards the poles.

124964.text: What do some bacteria produce from pyruvic acid during fermentation?
124964.sol: In fermentation, say by yeast, the incomplete oxidation of glucose is achieved under anaerobic conditions by sets of reactions where pyruvic acid is converted to CO2 and ethanol. The enzymes, pyruvic acid decarboxylase and alcohol dehydrogenase catalyse these reactions. Other organisms like some bacteria produce lactic acid from pyruvic acid . The steps involved are shown in Figure 12.2. In animal cells also, like muscles during exercise, when oxygen is inadequate for cellular respiration pyruvic acid is reduced to

125081.subject: Botany
125081.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: In the citric acid cycle, the continued oxidation of acetyl CoA via the TCA cycle requires the continued replenishment of oxaloacetic acid, the first member of the cycle. Reason: In addition it also requires regeneration of NAD+ and FAD+ from NADH and FADH2 respectively.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
125081.sol: In the citric acid cycle, the continued oxidation of acetyl CoA via the TCA cycle requires the continued replenishment of oxaloacetic acid, the first member of the cycle. In addition it also requires regeneration of NAD+ and FAD+ from NADH and FADH2 respectively.

125123.subject: Botany
125123.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. Glucose is the favoured substrate for respiration. 2. All carbohydrates are usually first converted into glucose before they are used for respiration. 3. Fats would need to be broken down into glycerol and fatty acids first. 4. The proteins would be degraded by proteases and the individual amino acids depending on their structure would enter the pathway
125123.sol: Glucose is the favoured substrate for respiration. All carbohydrates are usually first converted into glucose before they are used for respiration. Fats would need to be broken down into glycerol and fatty acids first. The proteins would be degraded by proteases and the individual amino acids depending on their structure would enter the pathway at some stage within the Kreb's cycle.

125834.subject: Botany
125834.text: What is claimed to be increased by pollen consumption?
options: Performance of athletes and race horses
125834.sol: Pollen grains of many species cause severe allergies and bronchial afflictions in some people often leading to chronic respiratory disorders– asthma, bronchitis, etc. It may be mentioned that Parthenium or carrot grass that came into India as a contaminant with imported wheat, has become ubiquitous in occurrence and causes pollen allergy. Pollen grains are rich in nutrients. It has become a fashion in recent years to use pollen tablets as food supplements. In western countries, a large number of pollen products in

126223.subject: Botany
126223.text: In some species of Asteraceae and grasses, a special mechanism has evolved to produce seeds without the fusion of gametes. What is this biological phenomenon called?
126223.sol: Although seeds, in general, are the products of fertilization, a few flowering plants such as some species of Asteraceae and grasses have evolved a special mechanism to produce seeds without fertilization, called apomixis. Parthenocarpy refers to the development of fruit without fertilization. Amphimixis is the normal sexual reproduction involving the fusion of male and female gametes. Polyembryony is the occurrence of more than one embryo in a seed. Answer: Apomixis

126434.subject: Botany
126434.sol: Parthenogenesis is a form of sexual reproduction in which the ovum develops into a new individual without fertilisation.

126602.subject: Botany
126602.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: When the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme, it is known as competitive inhibitor Reason: Such competitive inhibitors are often used in the control of bacterial pathogens.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
126602.sol: When the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme, it is known as competitive inhibitor. Such competitive inhibitors are often used in the control of bacterial pathogens

126962.subject: Botany
126962.text: The device which can remove particulate matter present in the exhaust from a thermal power plant is:
126962.sol: There are several ways of removing particulate matter; the most widely used of which is the electrostatic precipitator, which can remove over 99% of particulate matter present in the exhaust from a thermal power plant. It has electrode wires that are maintained at several thousand volts, which produce a corona that releases electrons. These electrons attach to dust particles giving them a net negative charge. The collecting plates are grounded and attract the charged dust particles.

127013.subject: Botany
127013.text: Step taken by the Government of India to control air pollution include :
options: Use of non-polluting Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) only as fuel by all buses and trucks
Compulsory mixing of 20 % ethyl alcohol with petrol and 20 % biodiesel with diesel
Compulsary PUC (Pollution Under Control) certification of petrol driven vehicles which tests for carbon monoxi
Permission to use only pure diesel with a maximum of 500 ppm sulphur as fuel for vehicles

127035.subject: Botany
127035.text: Industrial melanism is an example of:
options: darkening of skin due to smoke from industries
defensive adaptation of skin against ultraviolet radiations
127035.sol: The correct option is (3) Protective resemblance with the surroundings Industrial melanism refers to the evolution of dark body colors in animal species that live in habitats blackened by industrial soot. The phenomenon has been documented in numerous species that hide from predators by blending in with their backgrounds. Peppered moths provide one such example where because of their protective resemblance with the surroundings they survived better.

127120.subject: Botany
127120.text: How many genetically different strains of rice does India have?
127120.sol: A single species might show high diversity at the genetic level over its distributional range. The genetic variation shown by the medicinal plant Rauwolfia vomitoria growing in different Himalayan ranges might be in terms of the potency and concentration of the active chemical (reserpine) that the plant produces. India has more than 50,000 genetically different strains of rice, and 1,000 varieties of mango

127246.subject: Botany
127246.text: What are the reasons for conserving biodiversity?
127246.sol: Earth’s rich biodiversity is vital for the very survival of mankind. The reasons for conserving biodiversity are narrowly utilitarian, broadly utilitarian and ethical. Besides the direct benefits (food, fibre, firewood, pharmaceuticals, etc.), there are many indirect benefits we receive through ecosystem services such as pollination, pest control, climate moderation and flood control. We also have a moral responsibility to take good care of earth’s biodiversity and pass it on in good order to our next generation

127296.subject: Botany
127296.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The introduction of invasive weed species like carrot grass (Parthenium), Lantana, and water hyacinth (Eicchornia) poses a threat to native species by causing environmental damage. Reason: Co-extinctions can lead to the decline or extinction of invasive weed species.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
127296.sol: The Assertion is true as it correctly states that the introduction of invasive weed species like carrot grass, Lantana, and water hyacinth poses a threat to native species by causing environmental damage. However, the Reason is false because it claims that co-extinctions can lead to the decline or extinction of invasive weed species.

127595.subject: Botany
127595.text: What do plants and photosynthetic bacteria do with radiant energy from the sun?
options: Fix it to make food from inorganic materials
127595.sol: . Except for the deep sea hydro-thermal ecosystem, sun is the only source of energy for all ecosystems on Earth. Of the incident solar radiation less than 50 per cent of it is photosynthetically active radiation (PAR ). We know that plants and photosynthetic bacteria (autotrophs), fix Sun’s radiant energy to make food from simple inorganic materials. Plants capture only 2-10 per cent of the PAR and this small amount of energy sustains the entire living world. So, it is very important to know how the solar energy ca

127647.subject: Botany
127647.text: If 10,000 Joule of energy is assimilated by producers in an ecosystem than how much amount of energy will be present in biomass of tertiary consumer:
127647.sol: The number of trophic levels in the grazing food chain is restricted as the transfer of energy follows 10 percent law – only 10 percent of the energy is transferred to each trophic level from the lower trophic level. In nature, it is possible to have so many levels – producer, herbivore, primary carnivore, secondary carnivore in the grazing food chain. . .

127895.subject: Zoology
127895.text: What ability do frogs have that allows them to hide from their enemies?
127895.sol: Frogs can live both on land and in freshwater and belong to class Amphibia of phylum Chordata. The most common species of frog found in India is Rana tigrina. They do not have constant body temperature i.e., their body temperature varies with the temperature of the environment. Such animals are called cold blooded or poikilotherms. You might have also noticed changes in the colour of the frogs while they are in grasses and on dry land . They have the ability to change the colour to hide them from their enemies (cam

127944.subject: Zoology
127944.text: What structure joins the right atrium of a frog's heart?
127944.sol: The vascular system of frog is well-developed closed type. Frogs have a lymphatic system also. The blood vascular system involves heart, blood vessels and blood. The lymphatic system consists of lymph, lymph channels and lymph nodes. Heart is a muscular structure situated in the upper part of the body cavity. It has three chambers, two atria and one ventricle and is covered by a membrane called pericardium. A triangular structure called sinus venosus joins the right atrium. It receives blood through the major veins

128779.subject: Zoology
128779.text: What is the difference between plasma and serum?
options: Serum is plasma without water and proteins
Serum is plasma without minerals and hormones
Serum is plasma without the clotting factors
128779.sol: Fibrinogens are needed for clotting or coagulation of blood. Globulins primarily are involved in defense mechanisms of the body and the albumins help in osmotic balance. Plasma also contains small amounts of minerals like Na+, Ca++, Mg++, HCO3 –, Cl–, etc. Glucose, amino acids, lipids, etc., are also present in the plasma as they are always in transit in the body. Factors for coagulation or clotting of blood are also present in the plasma in an inactive form. Plasma without the clotting factors is called serum.

128965.subject: Zoology
128965.text: Identify the number of correct statements w.r.t given diagram. Electro-cardiogram is used to obtain this graph. ECG is a graphical representation of the mechanical activity of the heart during a cardiac cycle. This is a complex ECG. Each peak in the ECG is identified with a letter from P to T that corresponds to a specific electrical activity of the heart.
128965.sol: A patient is hooked up to a monitoring machine that shows voltage traces on a screen and makes the sound “... pip... pip... pip..... peeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee” as the patient goes into cardiac arrest. This type of machine (electro-cardiograph) is used to obtain an electrocardiogram (ECG). ECG is a graphical representation of the electrical activity of the heart during a cardiac cycle. To obtain a standard ECG, a patient is connected to the machine with three electrical leads (one to each wrist and to the left ankle)

129068.subject: Zoology
129068.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding the components of the blood coagulation cascade. List-I List-II A. Fibrinogen I. Enzyme complex that activates prothrombin B. Thrombin II. Soluble inactive protein in plasma C. Thrombokinase III. Essential mineral ion for clotting D. Calcium ions IV. Enzyme that converts inactive precursor into fibrin Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
129068.sol: According to NCERT, fibrinogens are soluble inactive proteins present in the plasma (A-II). Thrombin is the active enzyme that converts inactive fibrinogen into fibrin threads (B-IV). Thrombokinase is an enzyme complex formed by a cascade of reactions, which is required to convert inactive prothrombin into active thrombin (C-I). Calcium ions play a very important role in the entire clotting cascade (D-III). Therefore, the correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III. Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

129705.subject: Zoology
129705.text: In a mammalian nephron, the osmolarity of the filtrate changes from 1200 mOsmL ⁻¹ at the hairpin loop to approximately 200 mOsmL ⁻¹ by the time it reaches the distal convoluted tubule. Which specific permeability characteristic of the intervening segment allows this significant dilution of the filtrate?
options: It is impermeable to water but allows transport of electrolytes actively or passively.
It is permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes.
It allows the passive reabsorption of both water and electrolytes simultaneously.
It is completely impermeable to both water and electrolytes.
129705.sol: The segment connecting the hairpin loop to the distal convoluted tubule is the ascending limb of the loop of Henle. As the filtrate moves upward through the ascending limb, its osmolarity decreases from 1200 mOsmL ⁻¹ to 200 mOsmL ⁻¹ . This dilution occurs because the ascending limb is impermeable to water but allows the transport of electrolytes (actively or passively) into the medullary fluid. Thus, solutes are removed while water is retained in the tubule. The descending limb (which concentrates the filtrate) is

130040.subject: Zoology
130040.text: Incidence of Emphysema – a respiratory disorder is high in cigarette smokers. In such cases
options: The alveolar walls are found damaged
The plasma membrane is found damaged
The respiratory muscles are found damaged
130040.sol: The alveolar walls are found damaged in cigarette smokers.

130056.subject: Zoology
130056.text: Name the important parts involved in creating a pressure gradient between lungs and the atmosphere during normal respiration.
options: External Intercostal Muscles of the ribs
Internal Intercostal Muscles of the ribs
130056.sol: Diaphragm, External Intercostal Muscles of the ribs and Internal Intercostal Muscles of the ribs are the most important parts involved in creating a pressure gradient between lungs and the atmosphere during normal respiration.

130074.subject: Zoology
130074.text: During strenuous exercise, skeletal muscles require an increased supply of oxygen. Which of the following local changes in the muscle tissue environment facilitate the increased release of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin?
options: Increase in p CO ₂ , increase in H ^+ concentration, and increase in temperature
Decrease in p CO ₂ , decrease in H ^+ concentration, and decrease in temperature
Increase in p CO ₂ , decrease in H ^+ concentration, and decrease in temperature
Decrease in p CO ₂ , increase in H ^+ concentration, and decrease in temperature
130074.sol: During strenuous exercise, the metabolic rate of skeletal muscles increases significantly. This leads to a higher production of carbon dioxide (increasing p CO ₂ ), an accumulation of metabolic acids like lactic acid and carbonic acid (increasing H ^+ concentration or lowering pH), and the generation of more heat (increasing temperature). According to the Bohr effect, an increase in p CO ₂ and H ^+ concentration, along with an increase in temperature, decreases the affinity of haemoglobin for oxygen. This causes a

130143.subject: Zoology
130143.text: The vital capacity of lungs is equal to
130143.sol: The vital capacity is the maximum amount of air that can be expelled from lungs by forced exhalation after a forced inhalation. It is equal to the sum of tidal volume (TV), inspiratory reserve volume (IRV) and expiratory reserve volume (ERV). aligned VC & = TV + IRV + ERV & =500+3000+1100 & =4600 ml aligned

130157.subject: Zoology
130157.text: What cells in the human body exhibit amoeboid movement?
130157.sol: Movement is one of the significant features of living beings. Streaming of protoplasm in the unicellular organisms like Amoeba is a simple form of movement.Movement of cilia, flagella and tentacles are shown by many organisms. Animals perform locomotion for the search of food, shelter, mate, suitable breeding grounds, favourable climatic conditions or to escape from enemies/predators.The methods of locomotion performed by animals vary with their habitats and the demand of the situation. Cells in the human body exhi

130458.subject: Zoology
130458.text: What is the total number of bones present strictly in the hand region (comprising the wrist, palm, and digits) of a single human forelimb?
130458.sol: The hand region of a human forelimb consists of the wrist, palm, and digits. According to NCERT, the number of bones in these regions of one forelimb are: Wrist bones (Carpals) = 8 Palm bones (Metacarpals) = 5 Digit bones (Phalanges) = 14 Total number of bones = 8 + 5 + 14 = 27. The total number of bones in the entire forelimb is 30, which includes the humerus (1), radius (1), and ulna (1), but these are not part of the hand region. Answer: 27

131048.subject: Zoology
131048.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Menstruation only occurs if the released ovum is not fertilised. Reason: Lack of Menstruation may be indicative of pregnancy.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
131048.sol: Menstruation only occurs if the released ovum is not fertilised. Lack of Menstruation may be indicative of pregnancy.

131060.subject: Zoology

Reason: The embryo with 8 to 16 blastomeres is called a blastula.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
131060.sol: The mitotic division starts as the zygote moves through the isthmus of the oviduct called cleavage towards the uterus and forms 2,4,8,16 daughter cells called blastomeres. The embryo with 8 to 16 blastomeres is called a morula.

131520.subject: Zoology
131520.text: What is the role of introns in genetics?
options: They appear in mature or processed RNA
They do not appear in mature or processed RNA
They are loosely defined as regulatory genes
131520.sol: The coding sequences or expressed sequences are defined as exons. Exons are said to be those sequences that appear in mature or processed RNA. The exons are interrupted by introns. Introns or intervening sequences do not appear in mature or processed RNA. The split-gene arrangement further complicates the definition of a gene in terms of a DNA segment. Inheritance of a character is also affected by promoter and regulatory sequences of a structural gene. Hence, sometimes the regulatory sequences are loosely defined

131762.text: Which of the following is true with respect to AUG?
options: It codes for methionine in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes
131762.sol: AUG has dual functions. It codes for Methionine (met), and it also act as initiator codon.

131777.subject: Zoology
131777.text: The amino acid attaches to the tRNA at its:
131777.sol: The amino acid attaches to the tRNA at its 3′ – end which is the anticodon loop.

131895.subject: Zoology
131895.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): In eukaryotes, the primary transcript (hnRNA) can be directly translated into a polypeptide in the cytoplasm. Reason (R): The eukaryotic primary transcript contains both exons and introns, and lacks the protective 5' cap and 3' poly-A tail. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appr
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
131895.sol: In eukaryotes, the primary transcript synthesized by RNA polymerase II is called heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA). It contains both coding sequences (exons) and non-coding sequences (introns), making it non-functional. Therefore, it cannot be directly translated into a polypeptide. To become functional mRNA, hnRNA must undergo post-transcriptional modifications in the nucleus: splicing (removal of introns), capping (addition of methyl guanosine triphosphate at the 5' end), and tailing (addition of adenylate residu

132059.subject: Zoology
132059.text: What happened when Mendel self-pollinated the tall F1 plants?
options: Some offspring were tall and some were dwarf
132059.sol: Mendel then self-pollinated the tall F1 plants and to his surprise found that in the Filial2 generation some of the offspring were ‘dwarf’ ; the character that was not seen in the F1 generation was now expressed. The proportion of plants that were dwarf were 1/4th of the F2 plants while 3/4th of the F2 plants were tall. The tall and dwarf traits were identical to their parental type and did not show any blending, that is all the offspring were either tall or dwarf, none were of inbetween height

132505.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): A man with blood group O cannot be the biological father of a child with blood group AB, regardless of the mother's blood group. Reason (R): Blood group O individuals have the genotype ii and can only pass on the i allele, whereas a child with blood group AB must inherit an I^ A allele from one par

(A) is correct but (R) is not correct

(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
132505.sol: Assertion (A) is correct: A child with blood group AB has the genotype I^ A I^ B . This means the child must inherit the I^ A allele from one parent and the I^ B allele from the other parent. A man with blood group O has the genotype ii and can only produce gametes containing the i allele. Therefore, he cannot provide either the I^ A or I^ B allele required for an AB blood group child, making it impossible for him to be the biological father. Reason (R) is correct: It accurately states the genotype of blood group O

132694.subject: Zoology
132694.text: What was the observed proportion of moths in England before industrialization in the 1850s?
options: Equal numbers of white-winged and dark-winged moths
132694.sol: Before industrialization in the 1850s, there were more white-winged moths observed on trees compared to dark-winged moths.The explanation put forth for this observation was that ‘predators will spot a moth against a contrasting background’ . During post- industrialisation period, the tree trunks became dark due to industrial smoke and soots. Under this condition the white-winged moth did not survive due to predators, dark-winged or melanised moth survived. Before industrialisation set in, thick growth of almost whi

132912.subject: Zoology
132912.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding the convergent evolution of placental mammals and Australian marsupials. List-I (Placental Mammals) List-II (Australian Marsupials) (A) Anteater (I) Spotted cuscus (B) Lemur (II) Numbat (C) Bobcat (III) Flying phalanger (D) Flying squirrel (IV) Tasmanian tiger cat Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
132912.sol: According to NCERT, placental mammals in Australia exhibit adaptive radiation in evolving into varieties of such placental mammals each of which appears to be similar to a corresponding marsupial. This is an example of convergent evolution. The correct matches are: Anteater (Placental mammal) corresponds to Numbat (Marsupial). Lemur corresponds to Spotted cuscus. Bobcat corresponds to Tasmanian tiger cat. Flying squirrel corresponds to Flying phalanger. Answer: (A) - (II), (B) - (I), (C) - (IV), (D) - (III)

133529.subject: Zoology
133529.text: Which of the following statements regarding disorders of the muscular and skeletal system is incorrect?
options: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction.
Muscular dystrophy is a progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle mostly due to genetic disorder.
Gout is the inflammation of joints due to the accumulation of uric acid crystals.
Tetany is characterized by rapid spasms in muscles due to high calcium ions in body fluid.
133529.sol: The incorrect statement is the one describing tetany. According to NCERT, tetany is characterized by rapid spasms (wild contractions) in muscle due to low calcium ions ( Ca²⁺ ) in body fluid, not high calcium ions. Myasthenia gravis is correctly described as an autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction. Muscular dystrophy is correctly defined as the progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle mostly due to genetic disorder. Gout is correctly described as the inflammation of joints due to the accumula

133990.subject: Zoology
133990.text: Select the correct pair of microorganism and the product obtained from it.
options: Monascus purpureus - produces large holes in Swiss cheese.
Monascus purpureus - produces large holes in Swiss cheese.
Streptococcus - produces streptokinase which is used to remove clots.
Aspergillus niger - produces citric acid and butyric acid.
133990.sol: Statins produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus are used as blood-cholestrol lowering agents. Saccharomyces cerevisiae is used for making bread and ethanol. Aspergillus niger (a fungus) produces citric acid.

134613.subject: Zoology
134613.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Taq Polymerase is involved in PCR technique Reason: This enzyme remains active during high temperature, including denaturation of double stranded DNA
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
134613.sol: Such repeated amplification is achieved by the use of a thermostable DNA polymerase (isolated from a bacterium, Thermus aquaticus), which remain active during the high temperature induced denaturation of double stranded DNA. The amplified fragment if desired can now be used to ligate with a vector for further cloning

134636.subject: Zoology
134636.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. When you insert a piece of alien DNA into a cloning vector and transfer it into a bacterial, plant or animal cell, the alien DNA gets multiplied. 2. After having cloned the gene of interest and having optimised the conditions to induce the expression of the target protein, one has to consider producing it on a large scale 3. If any protein encoding gene
134636.sol: After having cloned the gene of interest and having optimised the conditions to induce the expression of the target protein, one has to consider producing it on a large scale. Can you think of any reason why there is a need for large-scale production? If any protein encoding gene is expressed in a heterologous host, it is called a recombinant protein. The cells harbouring cloned genes of interest may be grown on a small scale in the laboratory. The cultures may be used for extracting the desired protein and then pu

134710.subject: Zoology
134710.text: The restriction endonuclease EcoRI recognizes the palindromic sequence 5'-GAATTC-3'. Which of the following accurately describes its cleavage action on this sequence?
options: It cuts exactly at the centre between A and T by breaking phosphodiester bonds.
It cuts between G and A by breaking hydrogen bonds.
It cuts between A and T by breaking hydrogen bonds.
It cuts between G and A by breaking phosphodiester bonds.
134710.sol: EcoRI recognizes the palindromic sequence 5'-GAATTC-3'. It cuts the DNA strand a little away from the centre of the palindrome site, specifically between the bases G and A on both the strands. The enzyme achieves this by cleaving the phosphodiester bonds of the sugar-phosphate backbone. It does not break hydrogen bonds directly; rather, the hydrogen bonds between the complementary bases of the sticky ends separate subsequently. Therefore, the correct action is cutting between G and A by breaking phosphodiester bond

135059.subject: Zoology
135059.text: When is total number not an easily adoptable measure of population size?
options: When the population is genetically diverse
When the population is very small
When the population is huge and counting is impossible or time-consuming
When the population has a high reproductive rate
135059.sol: Although total number is generally the most appropriate measure of population density, it is in some cases either meaningless or difficult to determine. In an area, if there are 200 carrot grass (Parthenium hysterophorus) plants but only a single huge banyan tree with a large canopy, stating that the population density of banyan is low relative to that of carrot grass amounts to underestimating the enormous role of the Banyan in that community. In such cases, the percent cover or biomass is a more meaningful measur

6a13e469688ac6d0667aad68.subject: Biology
6a13e469688ac6d0667aad68.text: During the biochemical characterization of Griffith's transforming principle, it was observed that the transformation of non-virulent R strain bacteria into virulent S strain was inhibited by the addition of which of the following enzymes?
6a13e469688ac6d0667aad68.sol: Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty performed the biochemical characterization of Griffith's transforming principle. They purified biochemicals such as proteins, DNA, and RNA from heat-killed S cells to determine which molecule could transform live R cells into S cells. They observed that protein-digesting enzymes (proteases) and RNA-digesting enzymes (RNases) did not affect the transformation of the non-virulent R strain into the virulent S strain. However, digestion with DNase inhibited the transformation, proving that D

6a16f3277cfacf7984f86712.subject: Biology
6a16f3277cfacf7984f86712.text: In prokaryotes, the plasma membrane extends into the cell to form special membranous structures that can be in the form of vesicles, tubules, and lamellae. Which of the following is not a function of these extensions?
options: Facilitating DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells
Conferring motility to the bacterial cell
Increasing the surface area of the plasma membrane and enzymatic content
6a16f3277cfacf7984f86712.sol: The special membranous structures formed by the extension of the plasma membrane into the cell in prokaryotes are called mesosomes. These extensions are in the form of vesicles, tubules, and lamellae. The functions of mesosomes include assisting in cell wall formation, DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells, respiration, secretion processes, and increasing the surface area of the plasma membrane and enzymatic content. Conferring motility to the bacterial cell is the function of flagella, not mesosomes.

6a2a77bcfad2360f42564b7c.sol: Using Einstein's photoelectric equation, eV₀ = hc - hc ₀ For the first case: eV₀ = hc - hc ₀ For the second case: eV₀ 4 = hc 2 - hc ₀ Multiplying the second equation by 4 gives: eV₀ = 2hc - 4hc ₀ Equating the two expressions for eV₀ : hc - hc ₀ = 2hc - 4hc ₀ Rearranging the terms: 4hc ₀ - hc ₀ = 2hc - hc 3hc ₀ = hc ₀ = 3 Answer: 3

303525.subject: Physics
303525.text: A geostationary satellite orbits at a distance of approximately 36000 km from the surface of the earth. Determine the weight of a 120 kg equipment placed inside this satellite. The radius of the earth is 6400 km .
303525.sol: The weight of an object placed inside a satellite is its apparent weight, which is the normal reaction force exerted by the surface of the satellite on the object. In an orbiting satellite, both the satellite and the equipment inside it are in a state of free fall towards the Earth. The centripetal acceleration of the satellite and the equipment is provided entirely by the Earth's gravitational pull. Let g' be the acceleration due to gravity at the orbit. The equation of motion for the equipment is mg' - N = ma_c .

Therefore, no additional external force is required to make the block move down the incline. The required force is zero.

305859.text: A current loop of arbitrary shape is situated in a uniform magnetic field B . Determine the net magnetic force exerted on the loop.
options: Dependent on the shape of the loop
305859.sol: The magnetic force on a small current element d l is given by d F = I(d l B ) . The net magnetic force on the closed loop is F = d F = I(d l B ) . Since the magnetic field B is uniform, it is constant over the loop and can be taken outside the integral. F = I ( d l ) B For any closed loop, the vector sum of the displacement elements is zero, i.e., d l = 0 . Thus, F = I(0) B = 0 . The net magnetic force on any closed current loop in a uniform magnetic field is always zero.

6a7a1ff823d996ef2f92b748.text: An ionic solid MX crystallizes in a face-centered cubic lattice where anions X ^- occupy the lattice points and cations M ^+ occupy all the octahedral voids. If the edge length of the unit cell is 514 pm and the ionic radius of the anion X ^- is 181 pm , the ionic radius of the cation M ^+ is _____ pm .
6a7a1ff823d996ef2f92b748.sol: In a face-centered cubic lattice where anions form the lattice and cations occupy all octahedral voids, the structure is of the rock-salt ( NaCl ) type. In this structure, the cations and anions touch each other along the edge of the unit cell. The relationship between the edge length ( a ) and the ionic radii ( r_+ and r_- ) is given by: a = 2(r_+ + r_-) Given: a = 514 pm r_- = 181 pm Substituting the given values: 514 = 2(r_+ + 181) 257 = r_+ + 181 r_+ = 257 - 181 = 76 pm Answer: 76
